summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #423 (phase 39 branch: user-configurable vault parameters), then clean up and push.
summary.outcome: All 7 review threads addressed and resolved: 6 code fixes implemented, 1 marked not applicable. Main merged in, 3 merge conflicts resolved, tests and typecheck passing, CI failure from the min-retention change fixed and pushed.

repo: Phase 39 is 'user-configurable vault parameters'; the branch is docs/phase-39-context.
TEE IPNS key enrollment follows the pattern in StorageTab.tsx — must wrap keys before createAndPublishIpnsRecord calls.

The @cipherbox/core circular dep removal (commit 560c871fe) landed on docs/phase-38-context but was not yet on the phase-39 branch, causing vault-ipns.test.ts to fail import resolution until the merge.
pnpm lockfile format diverged between branch and main (inline vs expanded YAML style), producing ~15k lines of cosmetic diff on merge — functionally identical content.
Squash-merge to main will resolve lockfile churn without manual intervention.

code.finding: Retention days min was 1; changed to 0 to allow 'keep forever' per D-03 spec. This required updating the existing clamp(0)=>1 unit test in packages/core/src/__tests__/vault-settings.test.ts:54.
Missing TEE IPNS key enrollment before createAndPublishIpnsRecord; added wrapping following StorageTab pattern using teeKeys from auth store.
Retention days was sourced inconsistently; fixed to use vault settings store. Main had already refactored to getSdkClient().purgeExpired(), so the merge required combining both changes.
setTimeout was leaking on unmount; fixed by storing the timer ID in a useRef and clearing it in useEffect cleanup.
Copilot suggested implementing presets; marked not applicable as deliberate design simplification for this phase.
New test file created for deriveVaultSettingsIpnsKeypair (5 tests). Separated from vault-ipns.test.ts to avoid the pre-existing @cipherbox/core import resolution failure.
Test asserted clamp(0) => 1; broke in CI after min changed to 0. Updated to assert clamp(0) => 0.

workflow: When a branch is missing commits from a sibling branch (not yet on main), cherry-picking or manually porting the fix is required — merging main does not help if the fix hasn't landed on main yet.
Stashing in-progress review fixes before merging main, then popping post-merge, is a clean way to handle the merge-then-apply pattern.

CI failures on changed behavior (min value change) that break existing tests are easy to miss locally if the broader test suite passes — always check test assertions that directly test the modified constant.
GraphQL batch-resolve of review threads is possible but the transcript resolved all 7 in a single batched mutation call.

friction: vault-ipns.test.ts had a pre-existing @cipherbox/core import resolution failure that blocked the new tests from running in the same file, requiring a separate test file.
The fix for the circular dep (commit 560c871fe) was on docs/phase-38-context but not on the phase-39 branch, causing confusion about whether the failure was pre-existing or introduced.
Merging main caused ~15k lines of lockfile churn (YAML formatting style difference between branch and main pnpm versions), prompting user concern.
STATE.md was overwritten by the main merge with stale phase-38 state and had to be manually restored to reflect phase-39 progress.
User interrupted the commit flow to run pnpm lint:fix manually, then asked to merge main instead of continuing — required stash/merge/pop workflow.
CI caught the vault-settings.test.ts regression (clamp min change) that local test runs missed, requiring an extra fix-and-push cycle.
open_items: VaultTab.tsx:203 presets feature deliberately not implemented — marked not applicable for this phase but may resurface as a future request.
pnpm lockfile formatting divergence between branch and main should normalize after squash-merge but no explicit cleanup was done.
deriveByoConfigIpnsKeypair and deriveVaultKeyIpnsKeypair (sibling functions to the newly tested deriveVaultSettingsIpnsKeypair) still have no unit tests.
